links.narration_bridge: After thirty-five sleepless hours, Matthew Walker's team saw the amygdala — the brain's emotional alarm — fire sixty percent harder at everyday stress.

links.function: top-down emotional regulation and linking emotion to decisions
links.narration_bridge: Sleep loss weakens the calming connection from the medial prefrontal cortex — the front emotional brake — leaving the alarm unchecked.

links.function: gating sensory input and coordinating slow-wave sleep rhythms
links.narration_bridge: As the thalamus — the central sensory gatekeeper — shifts the cortex into synchronized slow delta waves, blood volume dips and clear fluid surges inward.
When overnight clearance stalls, sticky metabolic waste lingers longest around deep memory hubs like the hippocampus.

links.function: regulating slow norepinephrine arousal pulses and autonomic rhythms
links.narration_bridge: Deep in the brainstem, slow fifty-second norepinephrine waves gently squeeze brain arteries like a fluid pump — until sedatives flatten that pulse.
